subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Shoply)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@shoply.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Shoply)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking time today — great to meet you and Ben. I wanted to capture a short recap from our call, confirm the pain points you shared, and align on next steps so we can move to a focused tech deep-dive.

Summary of pain / goals you shared:
- Primary drivers: reduce unit cost and vendor lock-in from current OpenAI/Anthropic usage while keeping output quality equal or better.
- Latency target for chat/generation endpoints: p99 under ~300ms for short-turn dialogs; startup wants fast interactive experience.
- Embeddings: current pipeline uses OpenAI embeddings for search/relevance; you need a drop-in replacement compatible with existing vector stores.
- Compliance: customer data must remain within US cloud region; audit logs and KMS integration are required.
- Ops: prefer a managed option for initial rollout (to avoid large infra lift) with an eventual private deployment for regulated customers.

Current stack you described:
- Product/API layer calls OpenAI and Anthropic for text generation and chat via an abstraction layer.
- Embeddings flow: OpenAI embeddings -> Pinecone (managed) indexing -> similarity search.
- Orchestration: serverless endpoints + a Redis cache for short-term convo state.
- Volume: ~1.2M tokens/day across environments; peak concurrency ~250 requests/minute.

Compatibility and requirements:
- OpenAI-compatible API surface is preferred for fastest migration; minimal code changes to SDKs.
- Tokenization differences are a concern (we discussed prompt drift with non-OpenAI tokenizers).
- Embedding vector dims must match or be adjustable; you requested a migration path for vector re-indexing.

Model shortlist (initial suggestion):
- Smaller generation / chat: Llama 2 (7B/13B) and Mistral-instruct for parity testing.
- High-quality generation: Mistral 8x/Redwood-verified 13B/33B variants (depending on latency budget).
- Embeddings: Open-source instruction-tuned embedding models (eg. MTEB-compatible models or OpenAI-compatible embedding replacements like text-embedding-3-small analogs).

Success criteria for pilot:
1) Performance: match p95/p99 latency within 20% of current OpenAI baseline for priority endpoints.
2) Cost: demonstrable >30% unit-cost reduction at target throughput using batching & KV caching.
3) Quality: human eval on 200 prompt pairs (OpenAI vs open-model) with no more than 5% regression on top-line metrics.
4) Ops: ability to route traffic, measure token-level cost, and have audit logs/KMS enabled.

Proposed next steps:
- I will share a short discovery doc (attached) with the prompts & metric templates we discussed + a checklist for the pilot.
- Schedule a tech deep-dive with Rishi (SE) and Aditya (Solutions) to review tokenization, embedding compatibility, and an initial model test plan — suggested times below.
- You to share a representative prompt set, sample responses that show current failures (if any), and a scoped dataset for embedding re-index testing.

Suggested times for the deep-dive: Thu 23 Jul 9:00–11:00am PT or Fri 24 Jul 1:00–3:00pm PT — please let me know what works.

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap-20260722.pdf (recap + pilot checklist), shoply-current-stack.csv (what you shared on call)

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this migration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@shoply.io>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Shoply)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick recap — this looks right and is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency: p99 target of 300ms is ideal, but prioritizing p95 (interactive) is fine for pilot.
- Embeddings: dimensions currently 1536 (OpenAI). We can tolerate a re-index if you provide tools to migrate incrementally.
- Security: we need SOC2-aligned logs and KMS integration; we can share a list of compliance questions for Rishi to review ahead of the deep-dive.

We can do Thu 23 Jul 10:00am PT for the tech deep-dive — that works for Ben and our EngOps lead.

I'll attach the representative prompt set and a small sample of anonymized conversations from prod (coming in a follow-up email).

Best,
Alicia

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@shoply.io>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tech deep-dive notes & next steps — Shoply pilot

Thanks everyone for the session this morning. Notes from the call and immediate next steps: 

Notes:
- Tokenization: we ran a quick comparison during the call — Llama 2 (13B) and Mistral show ~2–6% token count variance vs OpenAI on your prompt set; this is manageable but we should adjust prompt prefixes and experiment with truncation/packing strategies.
- Embedding replacement: recommended to test two models (OSS-embed-1536 and a smaller cross-encoder for reranking). We'll provide a script to re-embed a small slice (10k rows) and validate similarity scores.
- Latency: initial inference profiles indicate 100–150ms per token on dedicated GPU infra for the 13B runs with batching; we still need to validate on your real concurrency patterns.

Immediate next steps:
1) Redwood -> deliver: a small pilot plan + minimal runbook (attachment: redwood-pilot-runbook.pdf) and a tokenization compatibility note.
2) Shoply -> deliver: representative prompt set and a 10k-row sample for embedding re-index.
3) Schedule a 1-week pilot (staged): dry-run validation -> 2-week live shadowing -> 4-week constrained traffic ramp.

I'll drop the runbook and scripts into the shared Drive folder (link sent in calendar invite).

Thanks — Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
